title: Make Something Wonderful: Steve's 2003 Stanford GSB talk on hiring A players and management by values
summary: In a 2003 talk to MBA students, Steve compares running Apple and Pixar and explains why Apple built its own retail stores. His core lessons: hire people far better than you, since the dynamic range of talent is enormous. Lead by "management by values", getting everyone to agree on the destination, and treat recruiting as the most important thing a leader does.

principles.text: Hire people better than you; the talent gap between average and best is huge.
principles.quote: The most important lesson I ever learned was that you have to hire people better than you are.

principles.text: A small team of great people can outdo hundreds or thousands of average ones.
principles.quote: I saw a team of fifty people do something that literally hundreds, or thousands, of people at other companies couldn’t do.

principles.text: Manage by values: find people who want the same things you do, then get out of their way.
principles.quote: What that means is you find people that want the same things you want, and then just get the hell out of their way.

principles.text: Agree on the destination, not the route; let each generation argue about how to get there.
principles.quote: So that each generation can argue anew about the best way to get to San Diego, and they’re not just taking your footsteps on how you got there.

principles.text: Make great products the goal; profit follows. Reversing the order makes things fall apart.
principles.quote: “We want to make a bunch of money, and so, OK, to do that, we’re going to have to make some good personal computers.” But it didn’t work. It never works.

principles.text: Recruiting is the most important thing a leader does; finding the right people is half the battle.
principles.quote: recruiting is the most important thing that you do. Finding the right people—that’s half the battle.
